# Bullet Rust SDK

> Rust and JavaScript/TypeScript clients for the Bullet trading API.

## References

- [Install and quickstart](README.md)
- [Rust API](https://docs.rs/bullet-rust-sdk)
- [JavaScript/TypeScript usage](wasm/README.md)
- [Runnable Rust examples](rust/examples/)
- [Node.js, Deno and browser examples](examples/README.md)
- [REST and WebSocket protocol](https://tradingapi.bullet.xyz/docs/)
- [Committed REST schema](rust/openapi.json)

## Integration gotchas

- Use the crate-root re-exports; separate interface dependencies are unnecessary.
- `Side::Bid` means buy; `Side::Ask` means sell. `NewOrderExt::ioc` creates an
  immediate-or-cancel order with a price limit, rather than an unbounded market order.
- Resolve symbols with `client.market_id()`. Metadata is cached at construction;
  call `refresh_metadata()` to discover new listings in a long-running client.
- Generated REST methods return `ResponseValue<T>`; call `into_inner()`.
  The `my_*` convenience methods unwrap responses and use the configured keypair's address.
- Price/quantity representation depends on the response: WebSocket depth levels
  are pairs of strings, while some REST fields are typed decimals. Consult the generated types.
- Read assigned order IDs from processed `PlaceOrder` or WebSocket `OrderUpdate`
  events, or set a `client_order_id` when placing the order.
- Client construction validates the exchange schema. `user_actions(...)` limits
  validation to the selected user actions and rejects other actions before signing.
- Use `UserAction::Transfer` for balance movement; the older deposit, withdrawal
  and sub-account creation actions are deprecated and rejected by the exchange.
- Transactions sign a versioned payload bound to the chain hash. For external
  signing, sign `UnsignedTransaction::to_bytes()`, never its display text. Solana
  wallets and Ledger use distinct signing formats; follow the API examples.
- `ManagedWebsocket` reconnects and replays subscriptions. Sends are queued;
  acknowledgements arrive as `WsEvent::Message`. `ManagedWsError::Busy` means
  command-queue backpressure; `Stopped` means the background task has ended.
- Managed idle detection counts application messages, not protocol ping/pong
  frames. Quiet subscriptions need application pings; see the WASM managed example.
- Rust REST failures convert to `SDKError`; use `is_retryable()` when choosing
  retry/backoff. WASM throws `BulletSdkError` with `kind`, `status` and `retryable`.
